 Error p.86 of qqplot book

Brad Horn <bxh...@gmail.com> Nov 01 08:53AM -0700  

Here is the code from the book:
 
(unemp <- qplot(date, unemploy, data=economics, geom="line",
xlab = "", ylab = "No. unemployed (1000s)"))
 
presidential <- presidential[-(1:3), ]
 
yrng <- range(economics$unemploy)
xrng <- range(economics$date)
unemp + geom_vline(aes(xintercept = start), data = presidential)
 
When I run the last line above, I do NOT get vertical lines as expected.
Instead I get the following error:
 
Error: Discrete value supplied to continuous scale
 
Why?

 

Brad Horn <bxh...@gmail.com> Nov 02 05:10AM -0700  

A simple reply confirmed that the start data used in the intercept argument
needs to be changed from a date to a numeric object. This faithfully
reproduces the example in the book.

 geo_vline: Error in example from ggplot2 book (p86)

Brad Horn <bxh...@gmail.com> Nov 01 11:13AM -0700  

The following code appears in the book (p86) and the book website to
illustrates the use of geom_vline:
 
unemp <- qplot(date, unemploy, data=economics, geom="line", xlab = "", ylab
= "No. unemployed (1000s)")
presidential <- presidential[-(1:3), ]
yrng <- range(economics$unemploy)
xrng <- range(economics$date)
unemp + geom_vline(aes(xintercept = start), data = presidential)
 
In my case, I geom_vline is generating the following error:
 
Error: Discrete value supplied to continuous scale
 
Logic says I shouldn't get this error. Any help or insight is appreciated
as I want to ensure the chart annotations are feasible.

 

Dennis Murphy <djm...@gmail.com> Nov 01 09:17PM -0700  

Hi:
 
> str(presidential)
'data.frame': 7 obs. of 4 variables:
$ name : chr "Nixon" "Ford" "Carter" "Reagan" ...
$ start: Date, format: "1969-01-20" "1974-08-09" ...
$ end : Date, format: "1974-08-09" "1977-01-20" ...
$ party: chr "Republican" "Republican" "Democratic" "Republican" ...
 
Observe that start is a Date object - you want the numeric equivalent,
because that's what is really plotted. This works for me in version 0.9.2.1:
 
unemp + geom_vline(aes(xintercept = as.numeric(start)), data = presidential)
 
Dennis

 Bug when plotting density plots for groups with one observation

Eric Stone <theeri...@gmail.com> Nov 01 12:46PM -0700  

Here's how I worked around it.
Before plotting your data, insert this filter to remove the rows with 1
dimension:
 
df <- subset(df, grouping.var %in% which (ddply (df, "grouping.var",
nrow)$V1 != 1) )
 
Then you can run the same plot command and it will work.

On 12-11-01 06:07 PM, Hermann Norpois wrote:
>> ggplot (huz)+ geom_rect(aes(xmin=s, xmax=e,ymin=0,ymax=p))
 
> Please give me a hint.

This is a computation of the width of your rectangles in relation to
the width of the plotting region:
 
with(huz,(e-s)/diff(range(c(s,e))))
 
The wider of the two rectangles is less than 0.2% of the width of the
plotting region -- less than one pixel ...
 
 

 

Winston Chang <winsto...@gmail.com> Nov 01 05:39PM -0500

"data.frame")

On 11/1/2012 4:31 PM, Winston Chang wrote:

 

Winston Chang <winsto...@gmail.com> Nov 01 04:48PM -0500  

Hm, maybe it's because I'm using the latest development version of ggplot2,
but mine doesn't have the hole in the middle when I use width=1.
 
Now that I think of it, with ggplot2 0.9.2.1, you might be able to make it
work by using scale_x_discrete(expand=c(0, 0)):
 
library(ggplot2)
dat <- data.frame(y = c(0.08, 0.92), g = c("A", "B"))
 
ggplot(dat, aes(x = factor(1), y = y, fill = g)) +
geom_bar(stat="identity", width=1) +
scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
coord_polar(theta = "y")
 
-Winston
